question: Does the classical modal signed-multiply-add representation improve complete resident FP64 Q1 actions by more than five percent against dense, symmetric-half and each of three libCEED CUDA backends on all six fixed primary cases?
scope: One RTX4090 allocation, CUDA12.6 sm89, eighteen correctness cases and six primary timing cases. A comparative isolated-action study, not a new mathematical method, optimizer speedup, convergence result, cross-device replication or current-toolchain claim.
selection_disclosure: Section79 rejected its signbit-specific all-controls claim. That exploratory comparison identified signed multiply-add as a candidate. This separate protocol tests that fixed candidate against physical-node and all three library controls with entirely fresh timings. The previous signbit claim remains failed; no old times are pooled.
library_release_scope: The retained section86 official release check identifies v0.12.0 as latest tagged release. Unreleased main development is not audited.

verification_sources.independent_assembly: Natural-grid element gather, dense Ke product and indexed assembly; it uses neither GPU tile ownership nor shared-memory reduction.

benchmark.analysis: Exact one-sided sign test on paired control/candidate host-wall ratios strictly above1.05; ties are nonwins. Holm FWER covers all30 fixed comparisons even if observations are missing. Each needs median>1.05 and adjustedp<=.05. All five controls on all six primary cases must pass, with every batch at least5ms.
benchmark.limitations: Twelve randomized blocks within one allocation do not establish independent-session replication. No favorable subset or adaptive stopping qualifies.

measurement: Every action clears reused output, assembles the same density-scaled element law, applies exact identity rows on the GPU and ends with cudaDeviceSynchronize. Host steady-clock batch time is primary; CUDA event time is secondary. Setup, input conversion, allocation, transfers, compilation, JIT warmup and numerical output are excluded uniformly. Fault-only context updates occur outside every timed block. Library arrays remain device resident during timing.
semantics: Natural library layout(z,y,x,component) and custom padded layout(x,z,y,component) represent the same physical nodes. The corrected eta/reflected-y restriction is inherited from section83. Each library operator uses one scalar density per cell and the qualified QFunction; identity rows now execute on GPU via paired device-vector access. This bridge and larger cases require fresh verification.
required: All18 primary and6 sanitizer processes,192 initial positive fields,192 post-timing fields,192 exact-zero fields after nonzero output,360 coefficient/boundary/geometry faults, actual device input roundtrips before and after timing, exact supports/identity rows and zero padding where present. All6 sanitizer summaries must be clean. Missing or failed execution fails the aggregate gate.

sanitizers.acceptance: Zero exit code plus an explicit zero-error summary; racecheck also requires zero warnings/hazards. All sanitizer-run numerical outputs are independently checked.

deployment.reason: Prefer currently eligible hosts that previously completed startup, upload and collection, then current total price. Do not select on numerical or timing outcomes. Preserve all recorded startup exclusions without causal hardware attribution.

deployment_upload.format: gzip level1 tar, regular files only
deployment_upload.verification: Each unique receiver attempt checks byte count and SHA256; remote assembly rechecks all chosen chunks and the full archive; every attempt is retained.

failure_policy: Build failure ends the numerical job. Individual process failures are retained while other declared processes continue within the absolute job timeout. No source, threshold, case, schedule or compiler edits and no numerical reruns on this rental. Any allocated-instance deployment failure ends this attempt; retain a separately declared retry if needed.
ownership: Only the fresh creation-response contract carrying jpdc-hex-libceed-resident-20260924 may be operated. Exclude every preexisting ID and user-owned52267803. Independent one-hour watchdog; destroy immediately after the complete archive and every member are locally hash-verified, before numerical replay.
compiler: Unchanged custom nvcc -O3 c++17 sm89 lineinfo defaults; bridge gcc O2 C11 fp-contract=off no-fast-math; libCEED unchanged make CUDA12.6 sm89 O3 fp-contract=off no-fast-math. Record version, commands, linked libraries, custom PTX/SASS/resources and binary hashes. No static-instruction eligibility filter or inferred dynamic bottleneck.
sdk_environment: Use the section87 proven CUDA12.6 math library tree, excluding stub directories. Require header/link/runtime probe and ldd without unresolved or stub library paths.
